subtitle: Where the Indo-Greek grid met the shrines of Gandhara

panels.shot: epic bird's-eye wide of a gridded city rising on a plain between hills
panels.action: Demetrius of Sirkap stands on a rocky rise overlooking a geometric grid of fresh streets and walls spreading across the Taxila plain, distant hills framing a sky of dust and pale light.

dialogue.text: On the Gandharan plain, Demetrius and his builders traced a Greek city in dust and stone—yet the shrines and streets of Sirkap would outgrow every plan they drew.

i18n.hi: गांधार के मैदान पर, दिमित्रियस ने धूल और पत्थर में यूनानी नगर खींचा—but सिरकप की गलियाँ और देवालय उनकी हर नक़्शे से आगे बढ़ गए।

panels.shot: low-angle medium on Demetrius beside a surveyor’s rope, distant Mauryan ruins behind
panels.action: Demetrius of Sirkap, in Hellenistic armour with a cloak, stands by surveyors stretching ropes over open ground, while far behind the older mound of Bhir shows broken mud-brick walls and abandoned lanes.

dialogue.text: North-west India, second century BCE. The old Mauryan streets of Taxila fall silent; to the north, an Indo-Greek king chooses open ground and orders a new city drawn tight as a net.

i18n.hi: उत्तर‑पश्चिम भारत, दूसरी सदी ईसा‑पूर्व। तक्षशिला की मौर्य गलियाँ सूनी पड़ती हैं; उत्तर में एक इंडो‑ग्रीक राजा खुला मैदान चुनकर नया नगर जाल की तरह खिंचवाता है।

panels.shot: overhead shot of surveyors marking a grid with ropes and stakes
panels.action: Seen from above, Demetrius watches engineers and local masons stretch taut ropes at right angles, fixing stakes into dusty soil to lay out long straight avenues forming neat rectangular blocks.

dialogue.text: Greek planners bring the Hippodamian grid to the Indian plain. A chessboard of streets appears in the dust: long north–south axes, cross-cutting lanes, rectangular insulae for homes, shops, shrines.

i18n.hi: यूनानी मंज़रकार हिप्पोडेमीयन ग्रिड भारतीय मैदान पर लाते हैं। धूल में शतरंजी सड़कें उभरती हैं—लंबी उत्तर‑दक्षिण धुरी, काटती गलियाँ, चौकोर मोहल्ले घरों, दुकानों, देवालयों के लिए।

panels.shot: wide shot along a future main street toward the city gate under construction
panels.action: From ground level, a straight avenue runs toward a rising city wall and unfinished gate, scaffolding clinging to stone bastions, while Demetrius rides slowly down the central line with guards and local chiefs.

dialogue.text: This new Taxila is Sirkap—‘severed head’—a fortified rectangle about a mile long, with thick stone walls, towers, and a main gate facing the hills. A frontier capital, planned from scratch.

i18n.hi: नई तक्षशिला है सिरकप—‘कटा हुआ सिर’—लगभग एक मील लंबा किला-सा आयत, मोटी पत्थर दीवारें, बुर्ज, और पहाड़ों की ओर खुला मुख्य फाटक। सीमा का नया राजधानी नगर, शुरू से योजनाबद्ध।

panels.shot: medium shot on Demetrius and an Indian elder in discussion amid building activity
panels.action: Demetrius stands in animated conversation with an older Indian householder wrapped in a cotton shawl, as behind them Greek and local workers raise stone courses and carve capitals in the sunlight.

dialogue.speaker: demetrius_i_and_the_builders_of_sirkap
dialogue.text: Your lanes, our grid. Let this be a city both of us can walk.

i18n.hi: तुम्हारी गलियाँ, हमारा जाल। ऐसा शहर बनाते हैं जहाँ दोनों साथ चलें।

panels.shot: interior street-level shot inside Sirkap, emphasizing right-angled crossings and drains
panels.action: Within Sirkap, a bustling straight street shows right-angled junctions, raised stone platforms, roadside drains, and rows of houses with simple facades; Demetrius rides past as vendors and craftsmen look on.

dialogue.text: Archaeologists will later walk these same lines—Marshall and Wheeler tracing drains and doorways, reading in stone the Greek taste for order joined to old Indian habits of courtyard and well.

i18n.hi: सालों बाद पुरातत्वविद इन्हीं रेखाओं पर चलेंगे—मार्शल और व्हीलर नालियाँ, चौखटें नापते, पत्थर में पढ़ते यूनानी क़ायदे को, जो जुड़ा है भारतीय आँगन और कुएँ की पुरानी आदत से।

panels.shot: tight medium on Demetrius holding a freshly struck coin, city rising behind
panels.action: Demetrius stands near a half-built wall, holding up a silver coin with Greek script and his diademed profile, while behind him the masonry of Sirkap’s fortification climbs under the hands of masons.

dialogue.text: Coins in Demetrius’ name, found in the lowest levels of Sirkap, fix the city’s birth to Indo-Greek ambition. A frontier kingdom stamps its image in silver—and in stone.

i18n.hi: सिरकप की सबसे निचली परतों में मिले दिमित्रियस के सिक्के नगर की पैदाइश को इंडो‑ग्रीक चाह से बाँध देते हैं। सीमा राज्य अपनी छाप चाँदी पर भी लगाता है—and पत्थर पर भी।

panels.shot: wide market scene along the main street, showing diverse traders
panels.action: A lively scene on Sirkap’s main street shows Greek-clad merchants, Indian traders in dhotis, Central Asian horsemen, and robed Iranians gathered around stalls of cloth, copperware and grain, with Demetrius passing in the background.

dialogue.text: Soon the grid fills with sound. Gandharan potters, Greek wine-sellers, Iranian traders, Saka horsemen. On this planned spine of streets, caravans from the Hindu Kush meet the villages of the plains.

i18n.hi: जल्दी ही ग्रिड गूँज से भर जाता है—गांधार के कुम्हार, यूनानी मदिरा‑विक्रेता, ईरानी व्यापारी, साका घुड़सवार। इन्हीं नापी हुई गलियों पर हिन्दूकुश से आए काफिले मैदानी गाँवों से टकराते हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a courtyard with a simple stupa beside a small shrine
panels.action: Inside a modest courtyard house, a small brick stupa rises beside a simple pillared shrine, lamps set before both, while a family prepares offerings in the evening light.

dialogue.text: Within the house-blocks, archaeologists find courtyards, wells, and tiny shrines. The grid may be Greek, but the inner life follows older rhythms—family, ancestor, local deity, all tucked behind strict lines.

i18n.hi: मोहल्लों के भीतर खुदाइयों में आँगन, कुएँ, नन्हे देवालय मिलते हैं। जाल भले यूनानी हो, भीतर की धड़कन पुरानी—परिवार, पूर्वज, स्थानीय देवता—सब सख्त रेखाओं के पीछे सिमटे।

panels.shot: epic medium-wide on the Double-Headed Eagle Stupa complex in a later phase
panels.action: In a later Sirkap street, the Double-Headed Eagle Stupa stands on a high base, its richly moulded facade bearing a carved eagle with two heads between pilasters, flanked by smaller shrines and stairways.

dialogue.text: Generations later, under Indo-Scythian and Indo-Parthian lords, Sirkap’s shrines grow elaborate. The so-called Double-Headed Eagle Stupa rises, mixing Indian stupa form with a motif with clear western echoes.

i18n.hi: पीढ़ियाँ बीतती हैं; इंडो‑स्किथियन और इंडो‑पार्थियन शासकों के तहत सिरकप के देवालय सजधज से भर उठते हैं। ‘दो‑सिर वाले गरुड़ वाले स्तूप’ की मीनार उठती है—भारतीय स्तूप देह पर साफ़ पाश्चात्य गूँज वाला चिह्न।

panels.shot: angled medium shot of an apsidal temple ruin within the city
panels.action: An apsidal, semi-circular ended sanctuary stands within the city, its stone foundations outlining a hall with a rounded apse, the interior floor worn smooth by long use.

dialogue.text: Nearby, apsidal sanctuaries appear—plans with rounded apses known in Indian Buddhist chaityas and in Hellenistic and Iranian cults. Sirkap becomes a notebook of overlapping sacred ground-plans.

i18n.hi: पास ही अप्सिडल मंदिर उभरते हैं—गोलाईदार अप्स वाले नक्शे, जो भारतीय बौद्ध चैत्य, हेलेनिस्टिक और ईरानी पंथों सब में जाने पहचाने। सिरकप पवित्र नक्शों की ओवरलैप होती कॉपी‑बुक बन जाता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of the Jandial temple outside the city walls with hills behind
panels.action: Outside Sirkap’s walls, the Jandial temple stands alone, a rectangular cella fronted by two tall classical columns, its stone blocks catching the sun with the hills of Taxila rising behind.

dialogue.text: Just beyond the wall sits the Jandial temple. Classical columns, a rectangular cella, inner niches. Scholars debate: a Zoroastrian fire temple? A Greek-style shrine? Its very ambiguity is part of the frontier’s story.

i18n.hi: दीवार के ठीक बाहर है जंडियाल मंदिर। शास्त्रीय स्तंभ, आयताकार गर्भगृह, भीतर कोटर। विद्वान पूछते रह जाते हैं—ज़ोरस्त्री अग्नि‑मंदिर या यूनानी शैली का देवालय? इसकी यही दो-मुंही पहचान ही सीमा की कहानी है।

panels.shot: cross-section style wide of a city block, showing mixed religious structures
panels.action: A cutaway view of a Sirkap block shows, side by side, a Buddhist stupa court, a small Hindu-style shrine, and a hall with column bases, all packed into one insula amid houses and shops.

dialogue.text: In one block, a Buddhist stupa courtyard. In another, a shrine with familiar Indian plans. Near them, halls with column bases hint at other cults. No single faith owns the grid; the city holds many.

i18n.hi: एक ब्लॉक में बौद्ध स्तूप‑आँगन, दूसरे में जान-पहचान वाला भारतीय नक्शे वाला देवालय। पास ही स्तंभ‑आधारों वाली सभागारें किसी और पंथ की ओर इशारा करती हैं। कोई एक मत इस जाल का मालिक नहीं; शहर सबको थामे है।

panels.shot: medium shot of an archaeologist’s hands brushing dirt from a coin and wall junction
panels.action: Modern hands with a brush and trowel clear soil from a coin lodged at the base of an old wall junction, revealing Greek letters while the weathered masonry of Sirkap emerges around it.

dialogue.text: Excavators in the twentieth century work down through levels of rubble. Early walls, Indo-Greek coins; above them, later rebuilds, new shrines, new street surfaces. The city is a stack of frontiers, not a single king’s design.

i18n.hi: बीसवीं सदी के उत्खननकर्ता मलबे की परतें काटते नीचे उतरते हैं। पहले की दीवारें, इंडो‑ग्रीक सिक्के; उनके ऊपर नई मरम्मतें, नए देवालय, नई सड़क सतहें। यह नगर सीमा‑स्तरों की परत है, किसी एक राजा की रचना नहीं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Sirkap’s ruined grid today, with tourists as tiny figures
panels.action: From a high vantage, the ruined grid of Sirkap stretches out in low stone lines and alleys, a few modern visitors walking like small figures among the sunlit foundations and shadows.

dialogue.text: Today Sirkap lies open to the sky, its walls knee-high, its shrines roofless. Yet the grid still guides the foot, drawing strangers into right-angled paths that once taught Greeks and Indians how to meet.

i18n.hi: आज सिरकप खुला आसमान तले पड़ा है—दीवारें घुटनों तक, देवालयों के ऊपर छत नहीं। फिर भी जाल अभी पाँव को साधता है, अनजान को उन सीधी गलियों में खींचता है जहाँ कभी यूनानी और भारतीय मिलना सीखते थे।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Demetrius’ face dissolving into the ruined streetscape
panels.action: Demetrius’ thoughtful face, half-shadowed, fills the frame before slowly dissolving into the empty, ruined main street of Sirkap lined with low stone walls under a clear sky.

dialogue.text: Demetrius is only the first name we can pin to this experiment. After him come Sakas, Parthians, Kuṣāṇas—each adding shrines, courtyards, facades—each learning that a city’s shape quietly trains its meetings.

i18n.hi: दिमित्रियस बस पहला नाम है जिसे हम इस प्रयोग पर टांग पाते हैं। उसके बाद साका, पार्थियन, कुषाण—सब नए देवालय, आँगन, मुखौटे जोड़ते हैं—सब सीखते हैं कि शहर की शक्ल चुपचाप मुलाकातों को ढालती है।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide of the grid fading into the surrounding fields and villages
panels.action: The straight lines of Sirkap’s grid fade into surrounding fields, tracks and villages, the ordered stone giving way to winding paths, as evening light softens the sharp geometry.

dialogue.text: Sirkap’s story reminds us that walls and streets are not neutral: on a Gandharan plain, a Greek grid once invited many worlds to cross paths, leaving a ruin that still teaches how space can shape encounter.

i18n.hi: सिरकप की कहानी याद दिलाती है कि दीवारें और गलियाँ तटस्थ नहीं। गांधार के मैदान पर यूनानी जाल ने कभी कई जगतों को एक‑दूसरे से टकराने बुलाया था, छोड़ गया ऐसा खंडहर जो अब भी सिखाता है कि जगहें मिलन को कैसे मोड़ देती हैं।
